questions.q: The temperature of a gas having $2 . 0 \times {10}^{25}$ molecules per cubic meter at $1 . 38atm$ (Given,  $k = 1 . 38 \times {10}^{- 23}J{K}^{- 1} )$ is :
questions.solution:
From ideal gas equation, $PV = nRT$

$⇒ PV = \dfrac{N}{{N}_{A}}RT$, where $N =$ total number of molecules

$⇒ P = \dfrac{N}{V}\left(\dfrac{R}{{N}_{A}}\right)T ⇒ P = \dfrac{N}{V}kT$

$⇒ 1 . 38 \times \left(1 . 01 \times {10}^{5}\right) = \left(2 \times {10}^{25}\right) \times \left(1 . 38 \times {10}^{- 23}\right) \times T$

$⇒ 1 . 01 \times {10}^{5} = 2 \times {10}^{2} \times T$

$T = \dfrac{1 . 01 \times {10}^{3}}{2} \approx 500K$

questions.q: Two thermodynamical process are shown in the figure. The molar heat capacity for process $A$ and $B$ are ${C}_{A}$ and ${C}_{B}$. The molar heat capacity at constant pressure and constant volume are represented by ${C}_{P}$ and ${C}_{V}$, respectively. Choose the correct statement.
questions.solution:
For process $A$:

$logP = \gammalogV ⇒ P = {V}^{\gamma}, ( \gamma > 1 )$

$P{V}^{- \gamma} =$ Constant

${C}_{A} = {C}_{V} + \dfrac{R}{1 + \gamma} \ldots \left(i\right)$

Likewise, for process $B \to P{V}^{- 1} =$ Constant

${C}_{B} = {C}_{v} + \dfrac{R}{1 + 1}$

${C}_{B} = {C}_{v} + \dfrac{R}{2} \ldots \left(ii\right)$

Also, ${C}_{P} = {C}_{v} + R \ldots \left(iii\right)$

By $\left(ii\right)$ and $\left(iii\right)$, we get

${C}_{P} > {C}_{B} > {C}_{v}$

questions.q: A block of ice at $- 10 ° C$ is slowly heated and converted to steam at $100 ° C$. Which of the following curves represent the phenomenon qualitatively:
questions.solution:
When the state of the substance is not changing, temperature of the substance increases when heat is supplied to it. But when the substance changes the state, the heat supplied to it used as latent heat and the temperature remains constant until all the substance converts to other state.

Therefore, temperature of ice first increases from  $- 10 ° C$ to $0 ° C$. Then, remains constant at $0 ° C$ till whole ice is melted. Then, it increases from $0 ° C$ to $100 ° C$. Again it remains constant at $100 ° C$ till whole water converts into steam.

questions.q: Two conductors have the same resistances at $0 ° C$ but their temperature coefficients of resistance are ${\alpha}_{1}$ and ${\alpha}_{2}$. The respective temperature coefficients for their series and parallel combinations are :
questions.solution:
Change in resistance due to temperature is given by, ${R}^{'} = R\left(1 + \alpha ∆ T\right)$

For Series Combination:

${R}_{eq} = {R}_{1} + {R}_{2}$

$⇒ 2R\left(1 + {\alpha}_{eq} ∆ T\right) = R\left(1 + {\alpha}_{1} ∆ T\right) + R\left(1 + {\alpha}_{2} ∆ T\right)$

$⇒ 2R\left(1 + {\alpha}_{eq} ∆ T\right) = 2R + \left({\alpha}_{1} + {\alpha}_{2}\right)R ∆ T$

$⇒ {\alpha}_{eq} = \dfrac{{\alpha}_{1} + {\alpha}_{2}}{2}$

For Parallel Combination:

$\dfrac{1}{{R}_{eq}} = \dfrac{1}{{R}_{1}} + \dfrac{1}{{R}_{2}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{\dfrac{R}{2}\left(1 + {\alpha}_{eq} ∆ T\right)} = \dfrac{1}{R\left(1 + {\alpha}_{1} ∆ T\right)} + \dfrac{1}{R\left(1 + {\alpha}_{2} ∆ T\right)}$

$⇒ \dfrac{2}{1 + {\alpha}_{eq} ∆ T} = \dfrac{1}{1 + {\alpha}_{1} ∆ T} + \dfrac{1}{1 + {\alpha}_{2} ∆ T}$

$⇒ \dfrac{2}{1 + {\alpha}_{eq} ∆ T} = \dfrac{1 + {\alpha}_{2} ∆ T + 1 + {\alpha}_{1} ∆ T}{\left(1 + {\alpha}_{1} ∆ T\right)\left(1 + {\alpha}_{2} ∆ T\right)}$

$⇒ 2\left[\left(1 + {\alpha}_{1} ∆ T\right)\left(1 + {\alpha}_{2} ∆ T\right)\right] = \left[2 + \left({\alpha}_{1} + {\alpha}_{2}\right) ∆ T\right]\left[1 + {\alpha}_{eq} ∆ T\right]$

$⇒ 2\left[1 + {\alpha}_{1} ∆ T + {\alpha}_{2} ∆ T + {\alpha}_{1}{\alpha}_{2} ∆ T\right] = 2 + 2{\alpha}_{eq} ∆ T + \left({\alpha}_{1} + {\alpha}_{2}\right) ∆ T + {\alpha}_{eq}\left({\alpha}_{1} + {\alpha}_{2}\right) ∆ {T}^{2}$

Neglecting small terms

$2 + 2\left({\alpha}_{1} + {\alpha}_{2}\right) ∆ T = 2 + 2{\alpha}_{eq} ∆ T + \left({\alpha}_{1} + {\alpha}_{2}\right) ∆ T$

$⇒ \left({\alpha}_{1} + {\alpha}_{2}\right) ∆ T = 2{\alpha}_{eq} ∆ T$

$⇒ {\alpha}_{eq} = \dfrac{{\alpha}_{1} + {\alpha}_{2}}{2}$

questions.q: P-T diagram of an ideal gas having three different densities $\rho_1, \rho_2, \rho_3$ (in three different cases) is shown in the figure. Which of the following is correct :
questions.solution:
For ideal gas $\begin{aligned} & P V=n R T \\ & P V=\frac{m}{M} R T \\ & P=\left(\frac{M}{V}\right) \frac{R T}{M} \\ & P=\frac{\rho R T}{M} \end{aligned}$ (Where $\mathrm{m}$ is mass of gas and $\mathrm{M}$ is molecular mass of gas)
for same temperature $\mathrm{P}_1>\mathrm{P}_2>\mathrm{P}_3$ So $\rho_1>\rho_2>\rho_3$

questions.q: A thermodynamic system is taken from an original state $A$ to an intermediate state $B$ by a linear process as shown in the figure. Its volume is then reduced to the original value from $B$ to $C$ by an isobaric process. The total work done by the gas from $A$ to $B$ and $B$ to $C$ would be :
questions.solution:
Work done during the path $A \to B$ can be written as $\begin{cases}{W}_{AB} & = & \dfrac{1}{2} ( 8000 + 4000 ) dyne{cm}^{- 2} \times \dfrac{1N}{{10}^{5}dyne} \times \dfrac{1{cm}^{2}}{{10}^{- 4}{m}^{2}} \times \left(7 - 3\right){m}^{3} \\ & = & 2400J\end{cases}$

The work done during the process $B \to C$ is given by

$\begin{cases}{W}_{BC} & = & \left(4000dyne{cm}^{- 2} \times \dfrac{1N}{{10}^{5}dyne} \times \dfrac{1{cm}^{2}}{{10}^{- 4}{m}^{2}}\right) \times \left(3 - 7\right){m}^{3} \\ & = & - 1600J\end{cases}$

Hence, the total work done is given by

$\begin{cases}W & = & {W}_{AB} + {W}_{BC} \\ & = & 2400J - 1600J \\ & = & 800J\end{cases}$

questions.q: During an adiabatic process, the pressure of a gas is found to be proportional to the cube of its absolute temperature. The ratio of $\dfrac{{C}_{p}}{{C}_{v}}$ for the gas is :
questions.solution:
It is given that

$P ∝ {T}^{3} ⇒ P{T}^{- 3} = \text{constant} . . . \left(1\right)$

For an adiabatic process,

$P{V}^{\gamma} = \text{constant} . . . \left(2\right)$

Assuming the gas to be a perfect gas, it can be written from equation (2) that

$P{\left(\dfrac{nRT}{P}\right)}^{\gamma} = \text{constant} ⇒ {P}^{1 - \gamma}{T}^{\gamma} = \text{constant} ⇒ PT\dfrac{\gamma}{1 - \gamma} = \text{constant}$

By comparing with equation(1), we get

$⇒ \dfrac{\gamma}{1 - \gamma} = - 3 ⇒ \gamma = - 3 + 3\gamma ⇒ 3 = 2\gamma ⇒ \gamma = \dfrac{3}{2}$
